- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.53) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.27) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for risk premium or market reversal.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 1–3 day decay filter to smooth out momentum-driven overreactions.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days above 75.00), model tends to hold too high; adjust downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven “late-cycle” corrections; if sentiment turns negative after 10–15 days, reduce forecast by 2–4% for final 5–7 days.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53) and price is trending upward; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment is “neutral to bullish”.
- If model forecast is >78.00 and sentiment is low, reduce by 3–5% to avoid overconfidence bias; if <70.00 and sentiment is high, increase by 1–2% to avoid underestimating momentum.
